stronger_arguments.description: If the analyst rev3 work on EXP-450 is non-trivial (operator notes 2026-05-31 HNOTE that H2 needs an aperture-sensitivity sentence with three numeric anchors at 500/1000/3000 km, and H4 needs alias-placement specification for three subsection ids), consider splitting: land P5 (Part 1 tier classification — independent, no H2/H4 dependency) and P6 (Part 1.1 overdetermined acknowledgement — uses EXP-476 corrected_p6 — no H2/H4 dependency) as a separate Phase-A integration commit, then land P0/P1/P2/P3 as Phase-B after rev3. This closes ISS-2273 immediately and unblocks operator-visible progress while the H2/H4 work proceeds. (Counter-argument the operator should consider: phased integration risks half-state cross-reference drift if part1 Tier 1 paragraph announces "Parts 1.5, 1.7, 1.8, 1.9, 2, and 2b" while Part 2 itself does not yet contain §2.13/14/15 — readers entering Tier 1 from the updated paragraph will not find the additional self-contradictions advertised, hurting credibility. Phased Phase-A might be NET NEGATIVE if Phase-B delays >1 week. Probably the right call is keep the integration atomic.)

kernel_of_truth.description: The operator's instinct to push a verification queue item after seeing the c08153e decider commit was operationally correct discipline. Pre-PROP-038 and Phase-1 of PROP-038 require curmudgeon verification of integrated rewrites before the decider closes the underlying ISSs. The error was reading the commit message label set (monitor/decisions/applied-patches/2026-06-02.json:entry[1] EXP-integration EXP-564 is unrelated to EXP-450; commit c08153e:message conflates EXP-450 H1/H7 fixes with EXP-450 P-patch integration) as evidence of integration. The general workflow — "after integration → verify → close ISSs" — is sound and is exactly what PROP-038 codifies. Note: this paragraph carries direct citations to source files per PROP-014 Mech 3 NARRATE-CITE discipline.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Sound workflow with the wrong premise produces a no-op verification, not a positive verification. The verification cannot be "clean" against a state that does not yet exist (see integration_state_check.expected_post_integration_artifacts in this review file — six per-patch absence findings from data/sections.json). A no-op verification logged as clean would set up the decider to close ISS-2273..2279 (open-issues.json:ISS-2273..2279) on a false premise, which would then surface as an integrity-agent finding ("ISS-2273 closed but the underlying hole still present in sections.json") within hours of the decider's next sweep. Reviewer-discipline cost of saying "premise wrong" up-front is lower than the cleanup cost of the integrity-trail unwinding. recommended_action_detail: The recommended action is on the WORKFLOW, not on the prose. There is no prose to rewrite because no prose has been integrated. Alternatively, treat this review as the verify-cannot-proceed sentinel and let the decider decide whether to (a) phase the integration per stronger_arguments.alternatives or (b) wait for rev3.
